model_checked.null_bound: Bernoulli mismatch with predictable/conditional probability p<=p0=0.005

validity_check.reason: At p=p0, E[factor]=p0*(p1/p0)+(1-p0)*((1-p1)/(1-p0))=p1+(1-p1)=1. For any p<=p0 and p1>p0 this expectation is <=1, so the product is a nonnegative supermartingale under the stated predictable conditional null. A fixed convex mixture of component e-processes is also an e-process.
validity_check.ville_alarm_bound: Threshold 100 implies crossing probability <=0.01 under the null, independent of the finite Monte Carlo sanity check.

independent_exact_recalculation.method: Absorbing dynamic program over (time t, cumulative mismatch count k). Because every likelihood ratio and the fixed mixture are functions only of t and k, first-crossing probability and conditional hitting-time quantiles can be computed without simulation or RNG.

interpretation: The worker's Monte Carlo operating characteristics are consistent with exact first-hitting calculations; discrepancies are sampling noise at the reported simulation sizes.

The null crossing probability is not merely observed below 1% in simulation: the e-process construction gives the <=1% Ville bound under the stated conditional null, and the exact finite-horizon probabilities above are about 0.41% and 0.49% for the two checked monitors.
The fixed mixture's broad detection behavior is quantitatively confirmed for the exact p0, p1-grid, threshold and horizons used here.
scope_guards: This does not validate any real serving system's mismatch rate or independence model.
The guarantee needs the per-step predictable conditional mismatch bound p_t<=0.005; arbitrary correlated bursts that violate that bound are outside scope.
Conditional hit-time medians/p90s are conditioned on an alarm occurring by the horizon and are not unconditional expected delays.
No claim is made that this p1 grid or threshold is optimal for other operational targets.
